name: Morgan

biography.name: Morgan

background.family: Lives with his father and stepmother; younger sibling shares the home.
background.finances: Moderate income; long professional study would need cost planning.
background.cultureLanguages: English; family enjoys discussing local news with differing opinions.
background.school: Public high school with debate and research assignments.
background.accessOpportunities: Library databases and teacher feedback; no legal practice exposure.

timeline.story: In 2014, Morgan liked retelling stories from the viewpoint of whichever character had been blamed. He also built block forts and occasionally changed the rules of entry so often that cousins refused to keep playing.

At six, he became interested in classroom rules and asked why exceptions existed. During 2017, a teacher helped him understand that a fair rule might still need different support for children starting in different circumstances.

In 2018, Morgan enjoyed comparing two accounts of the same historical event. He initially treated disagreement as proof someone was lying, then learned that perspective and incomplete information could produce different accounts without deliberate deception.

During 2020, he read widely and argued about news at home. His stepmother asked him to summarize the other person’s view before replying, a practice he found irritating but later useful in school discussions.

At twelve, Morgan joined debate and liked weighing evidence more than memorizing a dramatic opening. In 2023, he researched competing accounts for a school argument and discovered that one attractive claim rested on a weak source.

Across 2024 and 2025, he revised written arguments after feedback and became more comfortable speaking to classmates. Explaining rules and rights appealed more than selling products, while he knew little about the paperwork and responsibilities of actual legal work.

At sixteen in 2026, Morgan is comparing Texas college pathways, possible professional study, and paralegal work. He imagines a future home and occasional travel, but wants to see ordinary legal workplaces before assuming debate enjoyment predicts satisfaction or readiness.

ambitions: Compare professional study and paralegal work
He imagines a settled home, close friendships, and occasional travel alongside useful work.

biography.selfDescription: I like an argument more when I have to take the other account seriously. Debate has made me curious about law, but I have not seen enough ordinary legal work to know whether the daily responsibilities would suit me.
openQuestions: Would detailed case administration interest him?
How would he respond when advocacy requires representing a view he dislikes?
